de los Muertos parade, which will not be held FY 26, and carry funds over
 into FY 27 to be utilized for the FY 27 Dia de los Muertos event which will
bring the total funding available in FY 27 to $100,000.

through October 1, 2026. The cultivation tax rate is subject to an automatic
increase on October 1, 2025, per the Consumer Price Index (CPI) calculator
without City Council direction.

B5. Motion to request a one-time revision to the current Council District
Priority Funding fiscal policy relating to Special Events and Filming (SEF)
fundraising efforts for FY 26. Council Offices shall be responsible for
completing the Special Events Council Event Form, including obtaining the
required signature. On this form, the Council Office must provide SEF with
the event budget and the anticipated amount to be raised through
sponsorships to be able to proceed, but a specific Council letter or
Approved Project List fund transfer, committing District Priority Funds
(Divide by 9) shall no longer be required prior to event arrangements.

responsible for covering the remaining balance either from future Divide by
9, operating budget, or any other solution.

Tidelands Operating Fund Group in the Parks, Recreation and Marine
Department estimated in the amount of $185,000 by FY 25 year-end and
carried forward to FY 26 to support 10 Municipal Band events in the
Tidelands area, fully funding the Municipal Band for FY 26 along with
already received sponsorships, with a commitment to dedicated
fundraising efforts from councilmembers and Municipal Band supporters to
support funding gaps for all foreseeable future seasons beyond FY 26 and
align future events to account for funds secured, which may be at a
reduced level if fundraising is not successful.

Design and Permitting funding of $100,000 from Tidelands Operating Fund
Group to allow the funds to create one dedicated Pickleball court and one
dual striped tennis/pickleball court in Marina Vista Park, with the remaining
amount to continue to be available for Design and Permitting for additional
new facilities.

Services Department to prioritize $70,000 funding if available from the
opioid settlement proceeds to distribute Fentanyl Detection Kits, as

Council to appropriate funds identified, if necessary.

 Development and Opportunity Department to prioritize BID funding support

B10. Motion to request the City Manager to work with the Economic
Development and Opportunity Department to prioritize BID funding support
available through the Former Redevelopment Agency (RDA) Sale Proceeds

Group in the Parks, Recreation and Marine Department, offset by
unallocated Park Impact Fees, for focused revisioning and community
engagement over the long-term restoration and public access
enhancements at Willow Springs Park, which will further open space

Airport Department to continue the subsidized aviation fuel for the

crosswalk repainting, permanent speed feedback signage, improved

 Group in the Park, Recreation, and Marine Department to recognize savings

 associations, so that the program better supports a broader range of

to deliver affordable housing and the work of the land trust to date, while

disbursement of the $200,000 is contingent on substantial progress toward

projected to range between $0 to $150,000 instead of $440,000 as

$250,000 and up to $500,000 in settlement assistance funding as an

 Promotion Fund Group, providing a total of $100,000 to fund the Long

City’s General Fund Group operating reserves and contingency funds to
protect core public services and fiscal resilience in the face of potential

 higher density areas and traffic volume.
